title: When the Beat Drops, the Heart Follows: How Music Steers Mood
title_zh: 节拍落下，心跳跟随：音乐如何引导情绪
intro_zh: 本文约507词，围绕音乐如何影响情绪与身体展开，包含研究数据与日常建议，重点词约6个。

paragraphs.en: On a crowded subway at 8 a.m., a tired office worker puts on her headphones. Within a minute, her shoulders drop and her breathing slows. The song did not change her job or the traffic, but it changed how her body felt. Researchers now describe music not as simple background noise but as a tool that can soothe a tense mind within moments.
paragraphs.zh: 早上8点，在拥挤的地铁上，一位疲惫的上班族戴上耳机。不到一分钟，她的肩膀放松下来，呼吸也变慢了。这首歌并没有改变她的工作或交通状况，却改变了她的身体感受。如今，研究人员不再把音乐仅仅看作背景噪音，而把它视为一种能在片刻之间安抚紧张情绪的工具。

paragraphs.en: The body responds to sound quickly. Music with a fast tempo, around 120 to 140 beats per minute, tends to raise heart rate and energy, which is why gym playlists are full of it. Slower music, near 60 to 80 beats, can help people regulate breathing and pulse. In this sense, a playlist can work like a remote control for the nervous system. That is why a workout playlist can feel like a coach.
paragraphs.zh: 身体对声音的反应很快。节奏较快的音乐，大约每分钟120到140拍，往往会提高心率和能量水平，这就是健身房歌单里充满快节奏歌曲的原因。较慢的音乐，接近每分钟60到80拍，可以帮助人们调节呼吸和脉搏。从这个意义上说，歌单就像神经系统的遥控器。这也是为什么健身歌单能给人教练般的推动感。

paragraphs.en: Musical keys matter too. Western listeners often link major keys with happiness and minor keys with sadness. Yet sad music is not always unpleasant. A slow minor song can evoke tender memories and give listeners a safe space to feel low without being overwhelmed. Psychologists call this the 'sad music paradox': the music sounds sad, but the experience can feel comforting.
paragraphs.zh: 音乐的调性也很重要。西方听众常把大调与快乐联系起来，把小调与悲伤联系起来。然而，悲伤的音乐并不总是令人不快。一首缓慢的小调歌曲可以唤起温柔的记忆，给听者一个安全的空间去感受低落，而不会被情绪淹没。心理学家称之为“悲伤音乐悖论”：音乐听起来悲伤，但体验却可能令人感到安慰。

paragraphs.en: Personal memory gives music extra force. A song heard during a first summer job or a long train ride can bring back a whole scene: the light, the smell, the person beside you. For older adults with dementia, this effect can be powerful. Care homes increasingly use familiar songs from patients' youth to reduce restlessness and encourage conversation, even when other memories have faded.
paragraphs.zh: 个人记忆赋予音乐额外的力量。在第一次暑期打工或长途火车旅行中听到的一首歌，能带回整个场景：光线、气味、身旁的人。对于患有痴呆症的老年人来说，这种效果可能很强大。养老机构越来越多地使用患者年轻时熟悉的歌曲来减少躁动、鼓励交流，即使其他记忆已经消退。

paragraphs.en: Hospitals have tested music as a low-cost calming aid. A review of 26 studies found that patients who listened to music before surgery reported less anxiety than those who did not, and some needed fewer sedatives. The music was usually chosen by the patients themselves, played at a comfortable volume, and started about 15 to 30 minutes before the procedure. The effect was modest but consistent.
paragraphs.zh: 医院已经测试过音乐作为一种低成本的镇静辅助手段。一项涵盖26项研究的综述发现，术前听音乐的患者比不听音乐的患者报告的焦虑更少，有些人所需的镇静剂也更少。音乐通常由患者自己选择，以舒适的音量播放，并在手术前约15到30分钟开始。效果虽然温和，但很稳定。

paragraphs.en: The same song can affect two people differently. Culture, personality and past experience all shape response. Someone who grew up with piano lessons may feel calm at a Chopin nocturne, while another person finds it boring. Music apps now collect 'mood' labels and skip rates to guess what will lift or relax each user, though human taste remains hard to predict.
paragraphs.zh: 同一首歌对两个人的影响可能不同。文化、性格和过往经历都会塑造反应。一个从小上钢琴课的人听到肖邦的夜曲可能会感到平静，而另一个人则觉得无聊。音乐应用程序现在会收集“情绪”标签和跳过率，来推测什么能让每位用户振奋或放松，尽管人类的品味仍然难以预测。

paragraphs.en: For daily use, experts suggest building a small 'mood first-aid' playlist. Start with a track that matches your current state, then move gradually toward the feeling you want. If you are anxious, begin with medium-speed music before trying upbeat songs. Forcing yourself to listen to happy music too early can feel false and may not help. Keep the list short, about five to ten songs.
paragraphs.zh: 在日常使用中，专家建议建立一个小的“情绪急救”歌单。先听一首与你当前状态相符的歌，然后逐渐转向你想要的情绪。如果你感到焦虑，先从中速音乐开始，再尝试欢快的歌曲。太早强迫自己听快乐音乐可能会显得虚假，也未必有帮助。歌单保持简短，大约五到十首歌。

paragraphs.en: Music is not a cure for serious stress or depression, and it cannot replace professional care. But as a daily tool, it is cheap, portable and immediate. A few minutes of the right sound can soften a hard morning, steady a racing heart, or help a difficult feeling pass. Sometimes that is enough to begin again. No prescription is needed.
paragraphs.zh: 音乐不能治愈严重的压力或抑郁，也不能替代专业护理。但作为一种日常工具，它便宜、便携且即时。几分钟恰当的声音可以缓和艰难的早晨，稳定狂跳的心，或帮助一种难受的情绪过去。有时，这足以让人重新开始。它不需要处方。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Music is mainly useful for entertainment at parties.
Music can influence mood and the body in practical, measurable ways.
Sad music should be avoided because it makes people unhappy.
Hospitals should replace medicine with playlists.
questions.explain: 文章主要说明音乐如何影响情绪和身体，并介绍了节奏、记忆、医院应用和日常建议，因此B最全面。A过于狭窄，C与“悲伤音乐悖论”相反，D夸大了音乐的作用。

questions.q: According to paragraph 2, what does fast-tempo music tend to do?
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出，每分钟120到140拍的快节奏音乐往往会提高心率和能量水平，因此选B。A是慢速音乐的效果，C和D文中未提及。

questions.q: Why can sad music feel comforting to some listeners?
options: It always has a fast beat.
It lets them experience sadness in a safe way.
It is usually played in hospitals.
questions.explain: 第三段提到，缓慢的小调歌曲能唤起温柔的记忆，给听者一个安全空间去感受低落而不会被淹没，因此B正确。A与慢速小调矛盾，C和D无依据。

questions.q: The word 'evoke' in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: evoke意为“唤起、引发”，在句中与memories搭配，表示“唤起记忆”，与bring to mind最接近。write down是写下，turn away是转开，slow down是放慢。
